title: Interlock commandments: a lightweight framework to reduce OKR noise and speed cross-functional decisions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales, company-level OKRs collect too many incoming initiative asks and ad-hoc alignment meetings. Teams spend engineering and PM bandwidth clarifying intent instead of shipping. Goal: create a scannable, enforceable interlock framework ("Interlock Commandments") that reduces recurring clarifying meetings by 50% and shortens decision lead time for initiative approvals from two weeks to 3 business days.

Scope: company-level OKRs and initiative alignment across Eng, Product, Design, Research, and GTM. Not included: detailed team-level sprint planning or individual performance OKRs.

Deliverables: a one-page Interlock Commandments checklist, a triage rubric for initiative-fit (impact, effort, risk, dependencies), a lightweight intake template for PMs, a decision SLA matrix (who signs off and within what window), and a short training deck + onboarding script for Q2 planning.

Success metrics: reduce number of cross-org alignment meetings per OKR from average 6 to <=3; close rate for initiative approvals within SLA >= 80%; stakeholder satisfaction score >= 4.0 on post-rollout survey.

Trade-offs considered: guardrails must be lightweight to avoid bureaucracy; the rubric will be intentionally coarse to avoid false precision. We will iterate on thresholds after two quarters using data from the OKR dashboard.

Implementation plan: (1) Draft commandments and intake template (this ticket). (2) 2-week pilot with 4 initiatives nominated by Eng, Design, GTM. (3) Update playbook based on pilot feedback. (4) Roll out to leadership and published on Confluence with a one-pager and the intake form.

Key stakeholders: PM (owner), Eng leads, Design lead, Research lead, Finance ops (for capacity signaling), People Ops (for change comms).

Open questions: How strict should the decision SLA be for enterprise vs product-area initiatives? Do we need an exceptions queue? Should Dedicated & Private sales-driven initiatives get an expedited path?
